in_text_mentions: eveloped hearing loss after she rubbed the ear canal strongly with a cotton swab by herself. The next day, the patient visited our clinic due to the appearance of ear leakage. On examination, two central tympanic membrane perforations centered in the anterior lower quadrant were observed in the right ear. In the left ear, a large central tympanic membrane perforation of more than 3 mm in diameter was observed extending from the anterior upper quadrant to the anterior and posterior lower quadrants. Bilateral tympanic membrane perforations were thought to have occurred simultaneously (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Single otoscopic image of a human patient's tympanic membrane with a blue arrow pointing to a perforation, exactly matching the caption 'Tympanic membrane perforation seen through otoscope (blue arrow)' and the configured disease tympanic_membrane_perforation. The article title ('atypical presentation of ear and mastoiditis tuberculosis in a 5-year-old child') supports age_group child and an atypical clinical context; the perforation itself is attributed directly by the panel-specific caption. The dark defect appears bounded by tympanic remnants in the central pars tensa region, consistent with a central perforation (subtype assigned from visual appearance; location not explicitly stated in caption, hence moderate confidence). Orientation markers (AS/S/A/P/I), the blue arrow and a timestamp confirm this is an annotated real patient otoscopic view, not a diagram or third-party image. [raw subtype: central pars tensa perforation]
